blocks.title: Malus's law
blocks.text: The intensity I of plane polarized light after passing through an analyzer is directly proportional to the square of the cosine of the angle theta between the transmission axes of the analyzer and the polarizer: I is proportional to cos^2 theta, or I = I0 cos^2 theta, where I0 is the intensity of the incident polarized light (after passing through the polarizer).

blocks.alt: Unpolarized light passes a polarizer and becomes polarized light of intensity I0. It then meets an analyzer whose axis is turned through angle theta from the polarizer's axis, and the light that leaves has intensity I = I0 cos^2 theta. A note says all passes at theta = 0 and none at 90 degrees.
blocks.caption: Schematic of Malus's law (original diagram after Figure 8.7a).

blocks.text: Malus's law gives a mathematical relation between the intensity of the light incident on the first polaroid (the polarizer) and the intensity of the light obtained after passing through the second polaroid (the analyzer), as shown in Fig. 8.7(a). An analyzer is also a polarizer, placed after the first one. Rotation of the analyzer affects the intensity of the polarized light; it is used to further reduce the intensity of the light and to adjust it by adjusting the angle of the analyzer with respect to the polarizer.

Certain transparent crystalline materials, like tourmaline and calcite crystals, are capable of confining the vibrations of light waves to only one plane. Such materials are called polaroids, which have high directionality in crystal structure. Light can also be polarized by natural phenomena like reflection, refraction and scattering. If a piece of polaroid is rotated in front of a polarized ray of light, it causes a variation in the intensity of the light that gets through; the reason is the angle between the initial polarizer and the axis of the second polarizer.

When the incident polarized light of amplitude A0 strikes the analyzer at an angle theta, it is resolved into two components, A0 cos theta and A0 sin theta (Fig. 8.7b). The component A0 sin theta is absorbed in the analyzer. Since only A0 cos theta passes through the analyzer, the amplitude A of the transmitted light is A = A0 cos theta. Since the intensity I is the square of the amplitude A, I = A^2, or I = A0^2 cos^2 theta, and I = I0 cos^2 theta (since I0 = A0^2), where I0 is the intensity of the incident polarized light.

blocks.alt: The polarizer axis is vertical and the analyzer axis is turned through theta. The red amplitude A0 along the polarizer axis is split into a green component A0 cos theta along the analyzer axis, which passes, and a blue component A0 sin theta at right angles to it, which is blocked. A box says intensity goes as amplitude squared, so I = I0 cos^2 theta.
blocks.caption: Resolving the amplitude into A0 cos theta and A0 sin theta (original diagram after Figure 8.7b).

items: If theta = 0 degrees, then I = I0: the intensity transmitted through the analyzer equals the initial light intensity that passes through the polarizer.
If theta = 90 degrees, then I = 0: the light is extinguished completely, that is, no light is allowed to pass through the analyzer.

blocks.text: Light passing through crossed polarizers is stopped: a vertical polarizer passes only vertically polarized light, which a horizontal second polarizer then blocks (For Your Information). Looking through two polarizers when they are crossed, very little light passes through (Do You Know).

blocks.title: Optical activity
blocks.text: Optical activity is the ability of some substances to rotate the plane of polarization of light passing through them. The rotation is detected with a polarizer and an analyzer (Fig. 8.8).

Many crystals and solutions rotate the plane of polarization of light passing through them; such substances are said to be optically active. Examples are quartz crystals, cinnabar (HgS), sugar water, insulin and collagen. The amount and direction of rotation depend on the following factors:

items: The concentration of the substance (the amount of a substance present in a given quantity of a mixture or solution).
The distance the light travels through it.

blocks.text: Optical activity occurs due to the asymmetric shape of molecules in the substance, such as being helical. A few millimetres thickness of such crystals will rotate the plane of polarization by many degrees. Certain organic substances, such as sugar and tartaric acid, show optical rotation when they are in a solution; this property of optically active substances can be used to determine their concentration in the solutions. A sugar solution rotates the plane of polarization of the incident light so that it is no longer horizontal but at an angle theta; the analyzer then stops the light when rotated from the vertical (crossed) position by that angle (Interesting Information).

blocks.alt: Polarized light from a polarizer passes through a block of an optically active substance such as sugar solution or quartz. The light leaves with its plane of vibration rotated by angle theta, and the analyzer must be turned through the same angle to let it pass.
blocks.caption: Optical activity: an optically active substance between polarizer and analyzer (original diagram after Figure 8.8).

blocks.title: Example 8.2
blocks.text: Find the refractive index of a medium if the polarizing angle is 54.5 degrees. Solution: theta_p = 54.5 degrees, n = ?. As tan theta_p = n, n = tan 54.5 degrees = 1.4.

blocks.title: Example 8.3
blocks.text: Polarized light with an intensity of 75 W m^-2 passes through an analyzer with its axis at 30 degrees to the polarizer's axis. What is the emerging intensity? Solution: I0 = 75 W m^-2, theta = 30 degrees, I = ?. Using Malus's law, I = I0 cos^2 theta = 75 cos^2 30 degrees = 75 (0.866)^2 = 75 x 0.75 = 56.25 W m^-2.

blocks.title: Example 8.4
blocks.text: Polarized light with an amplitude of 5 units passes through a polarizer with its electric field aligned at 60 degrees to the original polarization direction. Find the amplitude of the wave after passing through the analyzer. Solution: A0 = 5 units, theta = 60 degrees, A = ?. Using Malus's law, A = A0 cos theta = 5 cos 60 degrees = 5 x 0.5 = 2.5 units.

items: Optics and photonics: polarization is essential for applications like polarized sunglasses, LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) screens and optical communication systems.
Imaging and microscopy: polarization enhances image quality, reducing glare (unwanted light that interferes with vision) and improving contrast, especially in microscopy and medical imaging.
Medical applications: polarization is used in cancer diagnosis, tissue imaging and laser surgery, leveraging its ability to distinguish between different tissue types.
Astronomy: polarization helps us to analyse cosmic phenomena, like the polarization of light from distant stars or the cosmic microwave background radiation.
Miscellaneous fields: optics and photonics, imaging and microscopy, biology and chemistry, communication systems, and so on.

blocks.text: Polarizers, also known as polarizing filters, have two main applications.

items: Sky photography: a camera used to photograph the clouds is fitted with a polaroid, which polarizes the light coming from the sky. Polarizers reduce the glare and haze produced by the scattering of light by small particles of molecules present in the atmosphere. They also enhance the contrast by blocking the excessively bright white light while allowing the other colours to pass through, creating a brighter, detailed image and improving the overall image quality.

Stress analysis of materials: in materials science polarizers are used to analyse the stress and strain on materials such as plastics, metals and glass. When a material is stressed its molecular structure changes, affecting the way it interacts with light, and interference fringes are formed which give qualitative information about the material. By shining polarized light through the transparent material and analysing the changes in its polarization, researchers can determine the material's stress patterns, identify potential weaknesses or defects, analyse its optical properties, and understand how it will behave under different conditions. This technique is known as photoelasticity and is widely used in engineering, materials science and quality control.

blocks.text: In both cases polarizers play a crucial role in manipulating light to achieve specific goals, whether enhancing image quality or analysing material properties. Polarized sunglasses act on the same principle: light waves reflected from a highway vibrate parallel to it and are blocked, while waves vibrating perpendicular to the highway pass.
